speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked	the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth with regard to heritage artefacts excavated by archaeologists or others in the last five years (a) whether all the artefacts have been properly documented and reported to the Government; (b) what is the legal ownership status of such artefacts; and (c) how are the artefacts stored and protected.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This includes most archaeological excavations conducted in recent years, such as the excavations at the National Gallery of Singapore in 2010 and Empress Place in 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Remaining artefacts may be stored by partner agencies, such as the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NHB has, nevertheless, worked closely with stakeholders to identify and protect important artefacts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: An example from the past five years would be artefacts recovered from the Cathedral of the Good Shepherd, which are owned by the Roman Catholic Church.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A number of artefacts recovered from the Cathedral are displayed at the Cathedral's Heritage and Resource Gallery.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Selected artefacts are also displayed at the Indian Heritage Centre, managed by NHB, for the public to access and appreciate.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NHB will seek feedback from stakeholders, such as archaeologists, heritage experts and non-government organisations (NGOs) in its review.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first is: what are the guidelines for the storage or protection of these artefacts for the partner agencies?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the same process of protection and storage applied to territorial waters in archaeological finds that are discovered in territorial waters?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And what happens when members of the public discover traces of archaeological finds, especially during property construction and renovation?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the Ministry going to consider imposing legal obligations for stopping work and reporting the finds to the Government?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: NHB will work very closely with the related agencies on the standard of protection and record keeping.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I must say that right now, we are working with very good professionals who themselves have a great interest in protecting the artefacts and there is a close collaboration on ensuring that the artefacts are well kept and protected for all to appreciate in the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are working closely also with MPA with regard to maritime archaeological finds.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We display maritime artefacts in the Asian Civilisations Museum (ACM), for example.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And with the support of philanthropists, such as the Khoo Teck Puat family foundation as well as Kwek Hong Png's family, we are able to have good displays for the public to appreciate such finds.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ultimately, I think we share the same common purpose.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is to understand the history of Singapore through archaeology.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And that history is really for the public, both present and future generations, to appreciate.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we want to keep artefacts as evidence of history for the benefit of many generations to come.
